structured_plan.G: Preparation only: no candidate program selected or assembled. Final G must be chosen from correctly validated, independently confirmed measurements.
structured_plan.analysis: Choose N=3. The supplied baseline is a serial row-column-k loop; for the timed sizes it uses the generic path, reads B with a strided access pattern, and does not use the threads argument. The distinct opportunities are an output-stationary SIMD kernel, an alternative B-transpose/packing strategy, and thread decomposition/scheduling without either custom SIMD microkernels or transposition. These cover the main independent algorithmic and scaling choices; a fourth tree would likely duplicate them. The baseline is valid with three reported times [0.134215, 0.132731, 0.133118] seconds (mean 0.133355, score 0.5). The supplied data does not give per-size/thread breakdowns or candidate comparisons, so it supports no speedup claim. Every candidate must handle all valid n, respect the thread budget, overwrite all of C, and pass the stated FP64 tolerance on signed inputs and fresh seeds; do not specialize to timed sizes.

children.objective: Explore a direct, output-stationary blocked GEMM: compute small C tiles with register-resident accumulators, contiguous row-major B loads, and SIMD across output columns; tune cache/register blocking and unrolling without transposing or packing B. Use disjoint output-tile ownership for any parallel work, bounded by threads. Keep n dynamic and verify correctness and wall-clock performance at both timed sizes and thread budgets, then retain a general path for all valid sizes.
children.subject: Direct register-blocked SIMD microkernel

children.objective: Explore the alternative of transposing or packing B into per-call scratch so each output dot product can use contiguous k-wise loads and SIMD reductions. Measure whether the transform cost pays off at the tested sizes and thread budgets; parallelize independent output rows or row groups within the threads limit. Do not reuse cached data or specialize to n=384/768. Check signed-input correctness against the FP64 tolerance, including the changed reduction order, and preserve a correct general-n path.
children.subject: Per-call B transpose/packing with k-wise SIMD reductions

children.objective: Focus on using the threads argument effectively with a compiler-vectorizable, cache-blocked row-major kernel, without explicit SIMD microkernels or B transposition/packing. Compare independent row slabs versus independent two-dimensional output tiles, static scheduling and parallel-region granularity; avoid races, oversubscription, and unnecessary launch overhead at one thread. Measure all timed size/thread combinations and preserve full output overwrite and correctness for every valid n.
children.subject: OpenMP work decomposition and thread-budget scaling
